name: Financial services
intro: Connect customer trust, operational resilience, and useful AI with controls that reflect the sensitivity of financial information.

cases.title: Coordinate investigation across critical services
cases.challenge: Security signals are fragmented across identity, endpoint, and cloud tools.
cases.approach: Map critical services to detection use cases, connect relevant telemetry, and define investigation and escalation playbooks.
deliverables: Detection coverage map and prioritized backlog
cases.measure: Triage quality, detection coverage, and overdue remediation.
cases.guardrail: Authorize containment explicitly; this is not a live incident-response service.

frameworks.reason: Use Detect and Respond outcomes to connect critical-service telemetry, investigation ownership, and exercised escalation.

cases.title: Prepare client information for secure Copilot use
cases.challenge: Broad collaboration permissions make confidential client content difficult to govern.
cases.approach: Review pilot repositories, assign information owners, and stage classification, sharing, and DLP improvements before broader AI adoption.
deliverables: Data protection and pilot readiness plan
cases.measure: Access gaps closed and pilot-quality acceptance.
cases.guardrail: Do not infer regulatory compliance from a product configuration.

frameworks.reason: Where client personal-data processing falls within GDPR scope, review purpose, access, retention, and approved AI reuse with privacy owners.
Link repository access reviews and information-handling evidence to the organization's defined information security management scope.

cases.title: Support relationship-manager preparation
cases.challenge: Account preparation requires searching multiple approved knowledge sources.
cases.approach: Design an assistant that assembles permission-aware background material with source references and explicit review before use.
cases.measure: Task usefulness, groundedness, and correction effort.
cases.guardrail: Keep investment advice, suitability decisions, and client commitments with authorized professionals.

cases.title: Unify governed management reporting
cases.challenge: Inconsistent definitions and disconnected data slow management reporting.
cases.approach: Create governed data products and semantic models with ownership, lineage, quality rules, and appropriate access.
cases.measure: Data freshness, reconciled definitions, and reporting rework.
cases.guardrail: Treat financial and regulatory reporting signoff as an accountable business decision.

cases.title: Protect hybrid-work advisory devices
cases.challenge: Advisory teams access sensitive systems from inconsistently managed devices.
cases.approach: Define enrollment, application protection, and endpoint baselines, then pilot access controls against approved advisory workflows.
cases.measure: Managed-device coverage and unresolved endpoint exceptions.
cases.guardrail: Preserve approved client-service workflows and validate access recovery before enforcement.

cases.title: Plan recovery for critical financial applications
cases.challenge: Application dependencies and recovery assumptions are not consistently documented or exercised.
cases.approach: Map service dependencies, agree on recovery objectives, and plan controlled recovery exercises for an authorized workload scope.
cases.measure: Recovery exercise outcomes and unresolved continuity gaps.
cases.guardrail: Business and risk owners approve recovery objectives; never test destructive actions against unapproved systems.

cases.title: Coordinate policy-change implementation
cases.challenge: Policy updates require manual coordination across control owners and business teams.
cases.approach: Route approved policy changes into owned implementation tasks with dependencies, review evidence, and exception escalation.
cases.measure: Overdue implementation tasks and evidence completeness.
cases.guardrail: Compliance professionals interpret obligations and approve policy changes; automation only coordinates approved work.

cases.title: Establish release gates for financial AI applications
cases.challenge: Teams lack consistent evidence for deciding whether an AI application is ready to release.
cases.approach: Define approved data sources, identity boundaries, evaluation datasets, and release criteria tied to the proposed application's consequences.
cases.measure: Evaluated releases, unresolved risks, and task-quality acceptance.
cases.guardrail: Keep lending, investment, and other consequential financial decisions under authorized professional oversight.

frameworks.reason: Map the application's consequences, measure task quality and misuse risks, and record accountable release and monitoring decisions.
Where the Act applies, classify the intended financial use and provider or deployer role before approving release; professional oversight alone does not establish compliance.

name: Healthcare and life sciences
intro: Protect sensitive records, support collaboration, and improve administrative workflows without treating AI as a substitute for clinical judgment.

cases.title: Govern a changing workforce's access
cases.challenge: Role changes, temporary staff, and external collaborators complicate access management.
cases.approach: Map responsibilities to access, establish sponsorship and review, and stage stronger authentication and privileged-access controls.
cases.measure: Overdue access reviews and unnecessary standing privilege.
cases.guardrail: Preserve tested emergency access and clinical continuity.

frameworks.reason: Use the Identity and Devices pillars to sequence workforce access improvements while retaining tested emergency access and clinical continuity.

cases.title: Improve sensitive-record handling
cases.challenge: Records move across collaboration tools with inconsistent classification and sharing.
cases.approach: Identify in-scope repositories, define handling requirements, and pilot labeling and DLP with privacy stakeholders.
cases.measure: Classification coverage and unresolved sharing exceptions.
cases.guardrail: Validate applicable privacy obligations, authorizations, and retention requirements separately.

cases.title: Assist administrative knowledge work
cases.challenge: Staff spend time locating current administrative policies and procedures.
cases.approach: Ground an assistant in approved administrative content, require citations, and test authorized and denied retrieval.
cases.measure: Answer usefulness, source freshness, and escalation quality.
cases.guardrail: Exclude diagnosis, treatment recommendations, and autonomous clinical decisions.

cases.title: Build a governed research data foundation
cases.challenge: Research teams need reliable data without uncontrolled reuse or sharing.
cases.approach: Design access-scoped data products with documented provenance, quality, ownership, and approved reuse boundaries.
cases.measure: Quality-rule coverage and timely authorized access.
cases.guardrail: Respect consent, purpose limitations, and review-board requirements where applicable.

frameworks.reason: Where research personal-data processing falls within GDPR scope, document lawful basis, sensitive-data conditions, permitted reuse, and transfer safeguards.

cases.title: Align security triage with care-service continuity
cases.challenge: Security investigations lack clear context about the services affected by proposed response actions.
cases.approach: Map in-scope business services to detection use cases and escalation owners, then exercise response recommendations with continuity stakeholders.
cases.measure: Investigation quality and documented response ownership.
cases.guardrail: Clinical continuity takes priority; containment affecting care systems requires explicit authorization and specialist input.

cases.title: Route administrative service requests consistently
cases.challenge: Nonclinical requests lose ownership as they pass between departments and support teams.
cases.approach: Map authorized administrative requests, connect approved records, and route work through defined queues, approvals, and exception paths.
cases.measure: Request age, repeated handoffs, and completion quality.
cases.guardrail: Do not automate clinical triage or access-to-care decisions through an administrative workflow.

cases.title: Evaluate nonclinical research AI applications
cases.challenge: Research support prototypes lack consistent data boundaries and evaluation evidence.
cases.approach: Design a bounded platform for approved nonclinical tasks with controlled sources, traceable evaluations, and reviewed release decisions.
cases.measure: Source validity, task quality, and unresolved release risks.
cases.guardrail: Respect study permissions and consent; exclude diagnosis and treatment recommendations from this scope.

frameworks.reason: Evaluate the approved nonclinical task, source limitations, and affected stakeholders before agreeing research-support release criteria.
Where the Act applies, assess the specific research use and organizational role rather than assuming every research activity is exempt or every health-related assistant is high-risk.

cases.title: Validate recovery of administrative platforms
cases.challenge: Administrative applications have undocumented dependencies and untested recovery assumptions.
cases.approach: Assess the authorized application scope, define recovery priorities, and plan nondisruptive exercises with clear ownership and rollback.
cases.measure: Recovery readiness and closure of critical dependency gaps.
cases.guardrail: Separate administrative testing from clinical systems and obtain approval for all production-impacting work.

name: Manufacturing
intro: Connect business systems, approved engineering knowledge, and operational reporting while maintaining deliberate safety and access boundaries.

cases.title: Create a trusted production reporting layer
cases.challenge: Operational and commercial reporting use inconsistent definitions.
cases.approach: Unify approved historical data into governed models with quality rules, ownership, and role-appropriate reporting.

cases.guardrail: Analytics do not replace industrial safety controls or operating procedures.

cases.guardrail: Do not extend business-system access controls into industrial control environments without specialist authorization.

cases.title: Improve recovery readiness for business applications
cases.challenge: Production-support business systems depend on aging applications with unclear recovery plans.
cases.approach: Assess dependencies, identify appropriate modernization treatments, and define recovery and cutover criteria for a bounded application portfolio.
cases.measure: Readiness gaps and validated recovery outcomes.
cases.guardrail: Protect plant continuity and keep safety-system changes outside the general application scope.

cases.title: Prepare engineering-office teams for Copilot
cases.challenge: Engineering-office staff want AI assistance but lack agreed knowledge and information-handling boundaries.
cases.approach: Select administrative tasks and approved engineering-office content, review access, and define a pilot with quality and adoption criteria.
cases.measure: Task usefulness, source accuracy, and readiness gaps closed.
cases.guardrail: Generated material requires professional review and cannot replace engineering validation or approved operating procedures.

frameworks.reason: If engineering-office content includes defense-contract information, establish the contractual CMMC scope and approved handling boundaries before connecting it to an AI pilot.
Define the pilot's administrative purpose, evaluate source accuracy, and retain professional review rather than treating generated content as engineering validation.

cases.title: Coordinate ransomware-response preparation
cases.challenge: Business IT teams have inconsistent detection, escalation, and recovery coordination.
cases.approach: Prioritize ransomware-related business threats, align relevant telemetry, and exercise approved investigation and escalation runbooks.
cases.measure: Coverage gaps, escalation clarity, and remediation age.
cases.guardrail: Exercises must not deploy live malware or disrupt production; industrial systems require separate specialist scope.

frameworks.reason: Connect Detect, Respond, and Recover outcomes through authorized ransomware table-top exercises without extending the business-system scope into industrial controls.

cases.title: Enable evidence-grounded campaign preparation

cases.measure: Draft usefulness, correction effort, and source accuracy.
cases.guardrail: Verify product and promotional claims; do not use customer data outside approved consent and purpose.

cases.title: Connect account-compromise investigation
cases.challenge: Identity and endpoint alerts lack consistent ownership across retail operations.
cases.approach: Correlate relevant security signals, prioritize investigation use cases, and document escalation paths for distributed business teams.
deliverables: Tuned use-case backlog and response runbooks
cases.measure: Alert quality, triage consistency, and unresolved gaps.
cases.guardrail: Access suspension and device isolation require approved procedures that consider store operations.

cases.measure: Coverage gaps, investigation quality, and remediation age.

cases.approach: Build governed data products with agreed measures, minimization, access controls, and documented lineage.

cases.title: Establish governed cloud landing zones

cases.title: Route administrative casework transparently

cases.title: Prepare staff for controlled document drafting

cases.title: Review cross-agency and contractor access

cases.approach: Assign sponsors, inventory in-scope access, and define periodic reviews and retirement triggers for partner identities.

name: Education

cases.title: Protect student records in collaboration

frameworks.reason: Where student-record processing falls within GDPR scope, document permitted purposes, access, retention, and applicable protections for children.

cases.title: Assist staff with administrative knowledge

cases.title: Coordinate campus service requests

cases.title: Protect customer data as the team grows
cases.challenge: Early collaboration patterns and expanding access create gaps in customer-information handling.
cases.approach: Identify sensitive information and accountable owners, review access, and stage classification and sharing controls for supported systems.
cases.measure: Excess permissions, owner coverage, and high-priority data gaps.
cases.guardrail: Do not claim certifications or compliance before appropriate assessment and evidence.

frameworks.reason: Where customer-data processing falls within GDPR scope, establish roles, permitted purposes, retention, and rights handling before scaling.
Define the management-system scope and ownership needed to sustain customer-data controls rather than treating a cloud configuration as certification.

cases.title: Take an AI product beyond a prototype
cases.challenge: A promising AI demo lacks a clear plan for data permissions, quality, reliability, and operating cost.
cases.approach: Define the product's permitted behavior, establish grounded context and scoped tools, and evaluate normal, denied, and failure cases before release.
cases.measure: Task quality, safe failure, latency, and cost per useful interaction.
cases.guardrail: A prototype is not production assurance; consequential actions and customer-data use require explicit authorization.

frameworks.reason: Map intended use and affected people, evaluate limitations, and establish accountable release and monitoring decisions beyond the prototype.
Where the Act applies, determine the startup's provider or deployer responsibilities, use classification, and effective obligations before placing the AI product into service.

cases.title: Make customer onboarding repeatable
cases.challenge: Sales-to-delivery handoffs rely on informal steps and repeated manual updates.
cases.approach: Map the onboarding process, integrate approved business records, and define ownership, approval thresholds, and exception routing.
cases.measure: Onboarding completeness, handoff effort, and exception age.
cases.guardrail: Keep contractual commitments, charges, and access provisioning subject to agreed authorization.

cases.title: Establish joiner and leaver access controls
cases.challenge: Fast team growth and contractor turnover leave excessive or ownerless access.
cases.approach: Define identity ownership, role-based access, strong authentication, and practical provisioning and retirement procedures.
cases.measure: Standing privilege and deprovisioning timeliness.
cases.guardrail: Preserve tested recovery access and avoid granting broad privileges for convenience.

cases.title: Create a proportionate incident-readiness plan
cases.challenge: Early-stage teams lack agreed security triage and escalation responsibilities.
cases.approach: Prioritize critical assets and available signals, define manageable investigation workflows, and exercise decision and communication paths.
cases.measure: Ownership clarity and high-priority coverage gaps.
cases.guardrail: Do not imply round-the-clock monitoring or emergency response without an explicit service arrangement.

cases.title: Build trusted product and customer analytics
cases.challenge: Product and commercial teams use inconsistent measures across disconnected data sources.
cases.approach: Define purpose-limited data products, agreed metrics, ownership, and quality checks for an initial reporting scope.
cases.measure: Metric consistency and reporting preparation effort.
cases.guardrail: Respect customer consent and privacy; avoid unnecessary individual profiling or unsupported investor claims.

cases.title: Enable useful internal Copilot workflows
cases.challenge: Teams want AI productivity without a clear view of data readiness and useful tasks.
cases.approach: Choose bounded internal use cases, review approved knowledge access, and pilot with guidance and explicit expansion criteria.
cases.measure: Task quality, sustained usefulness, and readiness gaps closed.
cases.guardrail: Protect customer and confidential company information and verify generated material before external use.
